Prefixes that show negative or opposite meanings
Use un- prefix before words that start with a vowel or consonant.
Use il- prefix before words that start with the letter “i.”: illegal.
Use im- prefix before words that start with the letter “m” or “p.”: impossible.
Use ir- prefix before words that start with the letter “r.”: irregular.
Use in- prefix with words that start with consonants and vowels, but not words that start with the
letter “i” or “u.”

Phrasal Verbs
Once upon a time, in a small village nestled by a glistening river, there lived a curious young girl
named Lily. Lily had always dreamed of embarking on a great adventure and exploring the world
beyond her little village.
One sunny morning, Lily woke up with an idea that had been brewing in her mind for quite some
time. She decided to set off on a journey to find a legendary treasure that was said to be hidden
deep within a mystical forest, far beyond the hills.
With her heart pounding and her backpack filled with supplies, Lily set out on her quest. She
walked through the village, bidding farewell to her family and friends, who wished her luck on
her adventure. As she made her way through the forest, she came across an old, weathered
signpost that pointed in different directions. It read, "Follow your dreams" and pointed towards a
narrow path.
Lily followed the path, which led her through dense thickets and over babbling brooks. She
climbed up steep hills and crossed treacherous bridges. At times, she felt like giving up, but she
reminded herself to keep pushing forward. She came across several obstacles along the way,
but she persevered and overcame each one.
Finally, after what felt like an eternity, Lily stumbled upon a clearing in the forest. In the middle
of the clearing stood a towering oak tree, with its branches reaching towards the heavens. And
beneath the oak tree, partially hidden by fallen leaves, was a gleaming treasure chest.
Lily's eyes widened with excitement as she approached the chest. With trembling hands, she
unlocked it using an ancient key she had discovered earlier in her journey. As the lid creaked
open, a radiant light poured out, illuminating the entire clearing. Inside the chest, she found not
just gold and jewels but also a note that read, "The real treasure is the knowledge and experience
gained on your journey."
Overwhelmed with joy and a newfound sense of accomplishment, Lily closed the treasure chest
and retraced her steps back to the village. She returned home, where her family and friends
eagerly awaited her arrival. She regaled them with tales of her daring adventures, recounting the
challenges she had faced and the lessons she had learned.
Lily's journey had transformed her. She had not only discovered a hidden treasure but also
realized the true power of determination, perseverance, and following one's dreams. From that
day forward, Lily became an inspiration to others in her village, encouraging them to step out of
their comfort zones and embark on their own remarkable journeys.
And so, the story of Lily, the young girl who chased her dreams and found her treasure, became
a legend that was told and retold for generations to come, inspiring countless others to set out on
their own phrasal verb-filled adventures.

Stumble upon:

Retrace one’s step:
Await:

1) Await (to wait for)
2) Stumble upon (to discover unexpectedly)
3) Retrace one's steps (to go back along the same path)
4) Overcome (to successfully deal with or defeat)
5) Step out of (to leave or depart from)
6) Walk through (to pass through)
7) Reach towards (to extend in a specific direction)
8) Set off (to begin a journey)
9) Push forward (to continue or persevere)
10) Set out (to start a journey)
11) Come across (to encounter)
12) Give up (to quit or stop trying)
